title: Strategy in Motion: How AI Is Supercharging War Gaming
gist: BCG argues AI makes war gaming broader and cheaper: a global health care client's post-workshop analysis covered 50+ scenarios, 350+ runs, 11,000+ actions and 400+ stakeholder-agent versions versus four groups pre-AI. It pushes multiagent simulation, always-on signal monitoring and human control of judgment, with a heavy equipment case where baseline strategy lost to bolder moves.

insights.claim: In a global health care company engagement, BCG modeled 50+ scenario permutations, 350+ simulation runs and 11,000+ actions using over 400 AI stakeholder-agent versions, versus four stakeholder groups in the same client's earlier pre-AI workshop.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Agent-based simulation raises scenario breadth by two orders of magnitude; consulting scenario work is shifting from workshop craft to compute-driven exploration.
insights.quote: a stark contrast to the four stakeholder groups represented in an earlier, pre-AI workshop

insights.claim: Traditional analog war gaming covers a handful of scenarios, whereas AI can generate dozens of additional future worlds, shifting the bottleneck from scenario generation to choosing which dilemmas deserve human time.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Value migrates to curation and prioritization of simulated outputs rather than generation.

insights.claim: Pre-game preparation for traditional war games can take weeks (choosing plotlines, synthesizing market, competitor and regulatory data, building persona briefings), and AI can dramatically compress it, though humans must still verify the inputs.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Time-to-insight compression lowers the cost of running strategy simulations, making them repeatable rather than one-off.

insights.claim: BCG argues that simulating stakeholders with separate AI agents holding distinct objectives, rather than one model playing every role, better captures friction and competitive dynamics of real ecosystems.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Single-model market simulations likely understate adversarial dynamics; architecture choice is a key diligence question for AI strategy tools.
insights.quote: not all AI is equal: architecture matters

insights.claim: In a heavy equipment manufacturer case, agents for the company, competitors, dealers, regulators and customers showed the baseline strategy consistently underperformed more ambitious moves, strengthening the case for decisive action.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Simulation outputs may systematically favor bold moves; treat such findings as vendor-reported and unverified, but indicative of consulting recommendations toward aggression.
insights.quote: the company’s baseline strategy consistently underperformed more ambitious moves

insights.claim: Multiagent war games identify contingent moves: opportunities pursued only when pre-established trigger criteria are met, alongside no-regret moves and big bets.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Decision output is a trigger-based playbook, linking simulation to if-then monitoring.
insights.locator: How War Gaming Strengthens Strategic Foresight

insights.claim: War games are powerful because participants playing competitors reveal incentives, biases, risk appetite and blind spots that data models and AI cannot fully replicate.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: AI simulation complements, not replaces, role-play; models trained on data miss idiosyncratic behavioral drivers.
insights.quote: reveal the incentives, biases, and blind spots that shape their behavior

insights.claim: Organizations often underweight competitor moves and countermoves because they are in love with their own plans or overtrust their models.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Model overconfidence is a named strategic failure mode; stress-testing against adversaries is undervalued.
insights.locator: How War Gaming Strengthens Strategic Foresight

insights.claim: BCG warns firms to resist letting AI control or own the war-gaming exercise, framing AI as assistive while teams still decide under pressure.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The advised governance stance is human-in-the-loop even for strategy simulation.

insights.claim: BCG recommends treating war gaming as a continuous capability, using AI to scan signals such as competitor moves, regulation, patent filings and customer behavior and to revisit scenarios and assumptions regularly.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Expect demand for continuous competitive-intelligence and scenario-monitoring tooling replacing episodic strategy offsites.

insights.claim: Organizations running continuous AI-assisted war gaming are claimed to move earlier and shape markets rather than react after the fact, though the article offers no quantified evidence.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Benefit claim is asserted, not measured; discount accordingly.

insights.claim: The best war games focus on one pivotal decision with few stakeholders, test multiple scenario variants, concentrate leadership time on key insights, and have executive ownership; vague goals like 'reduce costs' yield unfocused analysis.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Narrow, decision-specific framing is the main predictor of useful simulation output.
insights.locator: Getting the Most from AI-Enhanced War Gaming

insights.claim: AI should be used to test assumptions early without narrowing scope too quickly; the aim is exploring plausible paths, not confirming a predetermined outcome.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Confirmation bias risk rises when AI is used to justify preferred strategies.

insights.claim: The most valuable war-game output explains why outcomes occur, exposing cues and early-warning signs that should trigger future action, not only what happens.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Signal identification is the durable asset; monitoring triggers convert simulation into operations.
